messages:
matt.h: Hey — saw a customer workload spike with mem growth on long-context chat + continuous batching. Repro on staging, linking flamegraph below.
maya: Ugh. Is this the merge path where batches keep getting merged even when KV fragments are hot?
alex: I dug into traces: when a large ctx request arrives it pins a big set of KV fragments. ContinuousBatcher then merges new incoming small batches onto that head and we see HOLE blocking for ~50-120ms. During that time other shards can't reclaim and we get paging.
jordana: Can you paste the flamegraph / perf counters?
ci-bot: Upload: https://internal-artifacts.redwood/ci/artifacts/1718123456/kv-flamegraph.svg (size=842KB) :sparkles:
matt.h: From the flamegraph: most time in KVFragment::pin + MergeWindow::apply (hot path). Also noticeable time spent in fallback eviction (kv_shard::evict_page).
alex: Observed pattern: (1) continuous merge holds a headblock pointer; (2) large ctx pins many slots; (3) smaller batches get merged and wait on head; (4) eviction runs but can't free due to pins; (5) paging and mem growth.
maya: So fragmentation + pinning + HO head-of-line = memory slope. Did you check per-shard residency histograms?
matt.h: Yes — shard 3/7 shows 3x slot residency compared to baseline after 10k requests. Histograms: worst-case tail: 95th percentile residency time ~4.2s.
jordana: That aligns with user repro. Could be merge heuristics are too eager. What are current thresholds?
alex: Config bits: BatchMerger.max_merge_age_ms = 200, BatchMerger.max_merge_bytes = 64KB, KVFragment.pin_timeout_ms = 5000 (hard-coded).
maya: 5s pin timeout seems high for longctx scenario. Also merge_age 200ms is long when head is pinned and we have high QPS.
matt.h: Quick experiment idea: reduce max_merge_age_ms to 40ms and add a merge_size_bank that disallows merging when host_ctx_size > 8kB. Also make KVFragment.pin_timeout adaptive: pin_timeout = min(5000, 2000 + ctx_len_ms_estimate).
alex: Patch prototype attached:```diff
--- a/runtime/contbatch/merger.cpp
+++ b/runtime/contbatch/merger.cpp
@@
- const int kMaxMergeAgeMs = 200;
+ const int kMaxMergeAgeMs = FLAGS_merge_age_ms;
@@
- const int kKvPinTimeoutMs = 5000;
+ int KvPinTimeoutMs() { return std::min(5000, 2000 + EstimatedCtxLatencyMs()); }
```
jordana: Nice. We should also add a fast-path to break a merge if the head's KV pin count > threshold (e.g., 256). Otherwise head-of-line lasts forever under tail-heavy contexts.
maya: Agree. Also add metrics: contbatch.merge_break_reason and kvfrag.pin_count at break time. We need data before rolling out.
alex: I ran quick A/B on staging: reducing merge_age to 40ms dropped 95th residency from 4.2s -> 1.1s and eliminated the worst paging events. CPU overhead +2%.
matt.h: Any regressions on latency SLO for small infer?
alex: P50/P95 token latency unchanged for small requests. P99 improved slightly because eviction pauses were fewer.
jordana: Good. But need to ensure we don't increase model kernel thrashing. Could merge sensitivity to kernel selection cause secondary perf regressions? e.g., if we stop merging some batches, we might change batch sizes and preferred kernels.
maya: Let's add a kernel-aware merge veto: if BatchMerger.predict_kernel_change(new_batch, head) == true then skip merge. Simple check using kernel profile hash.
matt.h: I can add a logging hook to record kernel hashes when merge decisions happen. We'll collect for 24h.
alex: Also found a small bug in kv_shard reclaim path: when eviction fails due to pin, we were re-enqueueing the page without exponential backoff causing busy-loop checks. Fix: add backoff_backoff_ms = min(1000, 10 * attempts).
jordana: Great catch. That could amplify CPU and make mem churn worse.
maya: Action items: 1) matt.h push merge_age=40, merge_veto_on_hot_head=true, adaptive_pin_timeout experimental flag; 2) add contbatch.merge_break_reason metric and kernel-hash logging; 3) add backoff to eviction requeue.
matt.h: I'll open PR with flags and perf dashboards attached. PR will run 10% canary on staging heavy chat workload.
alex: Timeline?
matt.h: PR today, canary tomorrow, collect 24-48h of metrics.
jordana: Also add e2e repro script in /scripts/repro/ that simulates longctx + small tail batches at 300 qps. We need reproducibility.
maya: I'll add the script and a small harness to dump kv_shard residency histograms every 30s.
ci-bot: CI: test/contbatch passed (145s), flake in runtime/kv/test_eviction.cpp but not blocking.
matt.h: Thanks. If staging confirms, we'll roll to dedicated for more production-like load. Also document config knobs in ops runbook. :+1:
